# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs. Edit the code, not this file. -->

Every setting halite reads, which of the three programs reads it, what
it defaults to, and the section of SPEC.md that defines it.

A configuration file is YAML. Settings a program does not read are an
error rather than a typo that does nothing, so a key misspelled or put in
the wrong file is reported at startup:

```yaml
# /etc/halite/node.yaml
node_id: web1.prod.example.com
file_roots:
  base:
    - /srv/halite/states
pillar_roots:
  base:
    - /srv/halite/pillar
```

Salt's own names are accepted where they differ, with a warning naming the
halite spelling and the release the compatibility shim is removed in. See
SPEC section 28.3.

| `cloud_grains` | `false` | 14.1 | Collect cloud metadata grains. Opt-in, because it costs a round trip. |
